combo_label: The Pub × Silly English Things × Mr Men & Little Miss

entries.clue: A grand tea party, or the undignified squabble that erupts at one
Broad paving slab of the old floor, worn hollow by boots
Quarter of a pint in imperial measure, and what a fish breathes by
Silk-hatted gentleman of means, regarded from below with deep suspicion
Midwinter cider-orchard ritual of singing to the apple trees
Little Miss who will not budge an inch; mule-headed and set in her ways
Salted snacks in foil packets, pinned to a card behind the counter
Ten fluid ounces of beer, the measure a driver settles for
Diminutive Mr Men chap; also the size of drink below a medium
Sunday field sale run from open tailgates and borrowed pasting tables
Absent-minded Hargreaves chap who makes a sheep in the lane a goose in the rain
